closest_works.citation: Hay (2025), Reparative justice and the victim’s burden
closest_works.shared_claim: Private acceptance cannot settle all outsiders’ claims; public repair may remain incomplete.
closest_works.difference: Controlled countermodel contests inference from that incompleteness to defeat of local authority or independently grounded local duty; identifies missing coupling premise.

closest_works.shared_claim: Local directed powers coexist with non-directed outstanding obligations. Basic framework already exists.
closest_works.difference: Framework is credited, not novelty claim. Proposed result is specific correction to later Hay argument and scope of universal non-reoffending commitment.

closest_works.citation: Fabre (2023/volume21), The Duty to Accept Apologies
closest_works.shared_claim: Acceptance can have directed grounds; p15 denies community readmission account.
closest_works.difference: No general defense of her duty claim; isolate what multipartite objection must establish to undermine it.

limitations: Bounded web search and primary excerpts, not full corpus. Strong overlap with Bennett acknowledged. Novelty depends on defensible limited counterexample/correction to Hay rather than new theory; independent precheck required.
